This example is for the IVR7 (Icepack Vehicle Router 7) model. IVR7 is an advanced vehicle routing problem solver that is easily customisable to most use cases like pickup and dropoff, multi-depot, multiple time windows and fleet mix problems.

The example illustrates the usage of the data upload API as well as model versioning. It shows how to reference matrix data in a (potentially) versioned model or load overriding elements on a particular matrix directly (one can provide a complete matrix in this manner too). For ths example, we build a simple pickup/dropoff (similar to the basic model) and configure "open routing". This means that if a vehicle finishes its day at any node, it is then not supposed to cost the return trip home. So as a start, we need to separate the depot (Guinness Storehouse) from the vehicle home location by name. It's okay if it's at the same point (long/lat), but we're going to separate the identifier so we can control the distance/time matrix nicely.


### Data 

```{r}

data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')

number_pubs <- nrow(data)

```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates and quantities (amount added to a vehicle at each location).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}
data <- data %>% select(-c(pickupTime,dropoffTime)) %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)",
                           "Quantity (quantity)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:4))))

```

### Running the example

An R script with all the lines needed to run the example can be found [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/examples/blob/master/R/ivr7-5-advanced2.R).

The example uses the **iceR** package which will first need to be installed (see information [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/iceR)) and then loaded. Helper functions are also provided in a separate file and need to be read in.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)

source('ivr7-model-helper.R')

```


Execute the example as follows:

1. **Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivr7-kt461v8eoaif', configFile = '../config.json')
```


2. **Create the model, add some data to it and upload it (if preferred)**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Create the model
sr <- new (IVR7.SolveRequest)
model <- new (IVR7.Model)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')

# Configure the model and add the data to it (See ivr7-model-helper.R for details around some of the methods used below)
sr$model$dimensions <- make_distance_time_cap_dims()
sr$model$locations <- make_locations(data)
# Add the vehicle-home location
sr$model$locations[[length(sr$model$locations) + 1]] <- sr$model$locations[[1]]
sr$model$locations[[length(sr$model$locations)]]$id <- "vehicle-site"
# This just copies the Guinness Storehouse object and creates a new id.

sr$model$jobs <- make_job_time_cap(data, src = rep(1, nrow(data) - 1), dest = 2:nrow(data))
sr$model$vehicleCostClasses <- make_vcc_simple('vcc1', 1000, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 1, 3)
sr$model$vehicleClasses <- make_vc_simple('vc1', 1, 1, 1, 1)
sr$model$vehicles <- lapply(1:4, function(i){
  make_vehicle_cap(paste0("vehicle_", i), 'vc1', 'vcc1',
                   2000, # the vehicle capacity
                   "vehicle-site", # start location
                   "vehicle-site", # end location
                   7*60,  # 7 AM
                   18*60) # 6 PM
})
# We've created vehicles which need to start/end at "vehicle-site". Now we can make
# the last change which is to override the distance between locations and the "vehicle-site".
# We're only going to modify the distances FROM locations TO "vehicle-site". If you wanted to
# do complete line-haul outsourcing-style modelling, you could also do this for "vehicle-site"
# TO all alocations. For now, we'll just demonstrate the open routing case.

# Upload/submit the model via the data upload API (this API allows us to push just the data without anything else) OR upload it as part of the model
# NOTE: The data upload service will need to be enabled on your key
dataUpload <- TRUE # Set to FALSE if you don't want to use the data upload API
if(dataUpload){
  data_api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivrdata-o43e0dvs78zq', configFile = '../config.json')
  ts <- new (IVRData.TransitSet)
  for(i in 1:(length(sr$model$locations) - 1)){
    tv <- new (IVRData.TransitSet.TransitValue)
    tv$fromId <- sr$model$locations[[i]]$id
    tv$toId <- "vehicle-site"
    tv$value <- 0
    ts$transits<- append(ts$transits, tv)
  }
  # Upload the transit set.
  data_model <- new (IVRData.CachedTransitSet)
  data_model$transitSet <-ts
  rm(ts) # Delete it to illustrate the point
  # Push the model data to the API
  modelID <-  data_api %>% postSolveRequest(data_model)
}else{
  # Add the transit set directly in the model.
  ts <-new (IVR7.TransitSet)
  for(i in 1:(length(sr$model$locations) - 1)){
    tv <- new (IVR7.TransitSet.TransitValue)
    tv$fromId <- sr$model$locations[[i]]$id
    tv$toId <- "vehicle-site"
    tv$value <- 0
    ts$transits<- append(ts$transits, tv)
  }
}

# Add the new transit generators linked to those transit sets
tgen_d <- new (IVR7.TransitGenerator)
tgen_d$id <- 'custom_distance'
tgen_t <- new (IVR7.TransitGenerator)
tgen_t$id <- 'custom_time'
if(dataUpload){
  tgen_d$requestId <- modelID # Note, we're telling the API where to find the Transit-set data.
  tgen_t$requestId <- modelID # We can use the same one here as before because it's all zero :-)
  # We could upload another column of zeros, but there isn't much point.
}else{
  tgen_d$transitSet <- ts # Explicitly provide all the data.
  tgen_t$transitSet <- ts
}

sr$model$transitGenerators <- c(tgen_d, tgen_t) # Add the custom transit generators

# Tell the vehicles that they should use these transit generators.
t_attr <- new (IVR7.VehicleClass.Attribute)
t_attr$dimensionId <- "time"
t_attr$transitGeneratorId <- 'custom_time'
t_attr$transitCoef <- 1.0
t_attr$locationCoef <- 1.0
t_attr$taskCoef <- 1.0
sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$attributes<- append(sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$attributes, t_attr)

d_attr <- new (IVR7.VehicleClass.Attribute)
d_attr$dimensionId <- "distance"
d_attr$transitGeneratorId <- 'custom_distance'
d_attr$transitCoef <- 1.0
sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$attributes<- append(sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$attributes, d_attr)

sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$toString() %>% cat
# We now have a road network distance + time generator followed by a custom time and custom distance generator.
# The API will execute the transit generators in the order they appear and will override previous values with 
# new values (if they exist). So in this case, it will build a transit matrix using the road network, then overlay 
# the custom matrix which was uploaded with our data.

# Set the other relevant information
sr$solveType <- 0 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

```

3. **Submit the model to the API**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```


4. **Retrieve the model response**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```


5. **Look at the result**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Get the solve time
solveTime <- api %>% getSolveTime(requestID)
```

Solve time: `r solveTime`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr)
tab$edges %>%
  filter(toLocationId == 'vehicle-site') %>%
  select(fromStopId, toStopId,
         fromLocationId, toLocationId,
         distance_start, distance_end,
         time_start, time_end) %>%
  mutate(distance_delta = distance_end - distance_start,
         time_delta = time_end - time_start)

# The distance and time from the last stop to the vehicle-end point is zero.
# You'll notice there is, however, still a geometry associated with this movement, which is fine
# since you know that you can ignore these in whatever visualisation you put together, like this:
l <- tab
l$edges$geometry[l$edges$toLocationId == 'vehicle-site'] <- NULL
# Ee can probably highlight the first and last stops for each route too.
stopColors <- rep('black', nrow(l$nodes))
stopColors[l$edges$toStopId[l$edges$toLocationId == 'vehicle-site']] <- 'red'
leaflet() %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = l$nodes, lng = ~x, lat = ~y, color = stopColors, radius = 5) %>%
  addPolylines(data = l$edges$geometry)

# This makes sense because the stops which are farthest away from all the
# other nodes are typically the points at which the route should end (because you're saving the
# most in terms of distance and time). This is indicated by the red markers in this plot.
```
